caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This line plot illustrates coverage as a function of the number of completions (k), with the x-axis representing k on a logarithmic scale ranging from 2^0 to 2^8 (i.e., 1 to 256), labeled as "Number of completions (k)". The y-axis represents "Coverage" on a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Four data series are shown: Llama-3B (blue solid line with circular markers), Llama-3B + FT (dark green solid line with triangular markers), Llama-1B (light blue dashed line with circular markers), and Llama-1B + FT (light green dashed line with triangular markers). All four lines exhibit a monotonically increasing trend as k increases. At k=2^0 (1), Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT both start at approximately 0.42 coverage, while Llama-1B and Llama-1B + FT begin near 0.22. At k=2^8 (256), Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT reach approximately 0.92 coverage, whereas Llama-1B and Llama-1B + FT plateau at approximately 0.72 coverage by k=2^7 (128) with minimal further increase. The Llama-1B + FT line remains consistently above the Llama-1B line by approximately 0.05 coverage across the range, while the Llama-3B and Llama-3B + FT lines are nearly overlapping throughout.
